M2-HR is reported to contain δ-ferrite, α-ferrite and a martensitic-austenitic (α′+γ) phase, i.e. four distinct phases.

overall_structure.value: Hot-rolled M2 (Fe–8Mn–3Al–1Si–0.2C) microstructure comprising multiple phases: δ-ferrite, α-ferrite, and a very fine martensitic-austenitic (α′ + γ) phase. A significantly higher amount of ferrite, especially δ-ferrite, is present in M2 compared to the Si-free M1 steel, as expected from thermodynamic predictions owing to the presence of Si. XRD confirms the presence of ferrite/martensite and only a small austenite fraction (fγ = 5.7 %) in M2-HR.

unmapped_findings: The hot-rolled M2 sample (M2-HR) contains martensite, which formed in the steel during air cooling after hot rolling; this is supported by the calculated Ms temperature of 296 °C for M2-HR, which lies above room temperature.

The hot-rolled M2 sample shows brittle behaviour with a significantly high UTS (1055 ± 15 MPa) and very low total elongation (15.4 ± 0.8 %); its fractograph exhibits cleavage fracture features (river markings, plateaus and ledges) indicating crack propagation along parallel planes.
δ-ferrite in the M2 steel forms while soaking at 1100 °C before hot rolling, and some fraction of α-ferrite forms from γ when the steel is subjected to finish rolling temperatures around 900 °C.

Grain size distribution (Fig. 8b) reports M2 grains mostly in the ~0.25–0.5 μm bin (~92 %) with a small (~3 %) population near 1.5 μm, but this distribution is reported for the intercritically annealed samples (M2-IA), not for the M2-HR sample.
